Nosocomial pneumonia is often caused by different pathogens, such as Staphylococcus aureus or Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which are both options provided. While Streptococcus pneumoniae is a common cause of community-acquired pneumonia, it is less frequently the cause of hospital-acquired pneumonia in immobile patients post-stroke. Additionally, the explanation refers to an immunocompromised state post-stroke, which isn't necessarily accurate; instead, immobility may contribute to risk factors for pneumonia rather than immunocompromise per se.
